# IMSA GTD PRO — degradation

    lap_time = a_{car,driver} + n · tyre_age + eps

`n` is the **net within-stint slope**: tyre loss and fuel gain combined. Standard errors are cluster-robust by car with a `t(G−1)` reference, so an interval from a 7-car field is honestly wider than one from 20.

**47 race-seasons.** Median net slope **+0.0190 s/lap**, steepest +0.0771, flattest -0.0684.

**7 of 47 fit a negative slope** — a tyre apparently gaining time as it ages, which is not a measurement. The flattest is Road America 2022 at -0.0684. The cause is a diagnosed and unfixed omitted variable: the model carries no race-time term, so track evolution is attributed to tyre age with its sign inverted. Two corrections were built for it and both were withdrawn on real data — see [`track_evolution_omitted_variable.md`](../../cross_series/track_evolution_omitted_variable.md).

**Read every slope below as a lower bound on degradation.**

Fuel and degradation are separable in **2 of 47** races: teams change tyres at essentially every fuel stop, so `laps_since_refuel` and `tyre_age` move together after fixed effects and fitting both yields a collinear ridge. Only the net slope is reported.
